recent_posts.title: Exploring with agents with Amelia Wattenberger (Changelog Interviews #680)
recent_posts.summary: A podcast interview with Amelia Wattenberger, designer at Augment Code working on Intent, exploring how AI agents are reshaping developer workflows and tooling. Key topics include the identity crisis developers face as agents take over coding tasks, the evolution from autocomplete to chat to CLI back to UI, why Intent uses a workspace as its core primitive rather than a chat thread, tradeoffs between one-worktree-per-agent vs. one-worktree-per-task, and the argument that prototyping is getting easier while finishing software is getting harder.

recent_posts.title: Burke Holland on how Opus 4.5 changed AI coding workflows
recent_posts.summary: A podcast interview with Burke Holland, a GitHub Copilot team member who codes with AI agents daily. The conversation centers on how Claude Opus 4.5 represented a significant capability leap for AI-assisted coding, and how GPT-5.3 Codex is also living up to expectations. Topics touched on include AI agent workflows, the holiday-season Claude usage bump, and various developer tools and projects in the ecosystem.

recent_posts.title: The mythical agent-month (Changelog News #182)
recent_posts.summary: Changelog News #182 covers several topics: Wes McKinney's take on the 'mythical agent-month' concept in software development, a tool called Peon Ping for employing AI agents, Andreas Kling's explanation of why the Ladybird browser is adopting Rust, Cloudflare's new efficient MCP server, and Elliot Bonneville's argument that money is the only remaining moat in tech.

recent_posts.title: Selling SDKs in the era of many Claudes with Steve Ruiz from tldraw (Changelog Interviews #677)
recent_posts.summary: Steve Ruiz, creator of tldraw, joins the Changelog podcast to discuss building and selling SDKs around tldraw's high-performance web canvas. The conversation covers how SDK and infrastructure businesses are impacted differently by agentic AI compared to SaaS companies, the emerging era of internal tooling, what happens when LLMs are given access to an infinite canvas, and the broader excitement and anxiety around keeping AI agents productively busy.

recent_posts.title: Peter Steinberger joins OpenAI, ZeroClaw and MimiClaw updates, managing AI systems
recent_posts.summary: Peter Steinberger joins OpenAI. ZeroClaw offers an improved implementation approach. MimiClaw demonstrates AI capabilities on low-cost hardware. Steve Yegge shares insights on managing AI systems. The telnet protocol reaches end of life.

recent_posts.title: Han shot first with Brett Cannon (Changelog & Friends #128)
recent_posts.summary: Brett Cannon returns to discuss Python development, but the conversation begins with an extended discussion of pop culture topics including Star Wars viewing orders, TV series like Lost and Game of Thrones, science fiction books, and AI-generated voice technology. The episode covers both entertainment and technical Python topics in a casual, conversational format.

recent_posts.title: Building the machine that builds the machine with Paul Dix, co-founder & CTO at InfluxDB (Changelog Interviews #676)
recent_posts.summary: Paul Dix, co-founder and CTO of InfluxDB, shares his hands-on experience experimenting with AI coding agents in real-world development scenarios. He discusses which agent-assisted workflows made it to production, which didn't work out, and why he's temporarily returned to manual coding. The conversation explores practical lessons learned from adapting development processes to an agentic world.

recent_posts.title: Vouch for an open source web of trust (Changelog News #180)
recent_posts.summary: Mitchell Hashimoto introduces a trust management system for open source projects. Nicholas Carlini experiments with Claude AI building a C compiler. Stephan Schwab explores the history of attempts to replace developers with automation. NanClaw emerges as an alternative to OpenClaw. Sophie Koonin shares skepticism about widespread LLM-generated content adoption.

recent_posts.title: It's a renaissance woman's world featuring Amal Hussein (Changelog & Friends #127)
recent_posts.summary: Amal Hussein discusses her new role at Istari, working in aerospace beyond traditional web development. She shares insights about helping ambitious aerospace organizations, the current state of the Software Development Life Cycle in 2026, and her experiences working outside the browser environment.

recent_posts.title: Setting Docker Hardened Images free featuring Tushar Jain from Docker (Changelog Interviews #675)
recent_posts.summary: Docker Hardened Images (DHI) are secure, minimal, production-ready container images that Docker launched in May 2025 and made freely available and open source in December 2025. This podcast interview with Tushar Jain, Docker's EVP of Engineering, explores the motivation, implementation, and benefits of these hardened images for developers building containerized applications.
